title: Centaurus A (MIRI image)
caption: The galaxy Centaurus A, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: Centaurus A · constellation Centaurus · about 11 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI. Image Processing: A. Pagan (STScI), J. Depasquale (STScI), M. Garcia Marin (ESA Office at STScI)

recognition.text: Ranked #17 on ESA/Webb’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: A galaxy stretches horizontally across a field of tiny purple, pink and white points. Its brilliant white and pale pink centre throws out eight diffraction spikes, loops of pink and lavender arc above and below it in an S shape, and a grey and white band of dust cuts across the middle. This is Centaurus A, about 11 million light-years away, seen by Webb's Mid-Infrared Instrument.
In visible light, thick lanes of dust hide much of this galaxy. Webb's infrared vision passes through them and reveals filaments, loops and glowing clouds of warm dust spread across the centre.

At the heart sits a supermassive black hole that is actively feeding and shines brightly. The tangled structures around it were shaped by a collision between galaxies in the past, and by activity that continues today. Farther out, the galaxy's edges fade into soft, feathery plumes reaching toward both sides of the frame.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (8.31 x 3.44 arcminutes) and distance (11 million light years), the frame spans roughly 27,000 × 11,000 light-years. Its light set out about 11 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Webb's Mid-Infrared Instrument observed in mid-infrared light. Blue shows the shortest filter, cyan traces PAH dust emission and red a silicate-dust filter.
understand.eye: Mid-infrared light is invisible to the eye, and it passes through dust lanes that block much of this galaxy in visible light.

explore: Mottled patches and bright knots are scattered along the dusty band. Around the galaxy, a few bright foreground stars show Webb's distinctive diffraction spikes, while countless fainter stars speckle the dark background.
alt: A horizontal galaxy with a bright white and pink centre with eight diffraction spikes, pink and lavender loops forming an S shape, and a grey-white dust band across the middle, on a background of tiny purple, pink and white points.
